data.body: Phase 1 RCA confirmed on clean origin/main 72731d3745. The byte-equivalence oracle at tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py:65-94 launches a second real Pandoc process for every prepared unit, and at line 81 it reads the live production _PANDOC_TO constant. The assertion at lines 433-454 therefore compares two processes configured by the same mutable production constants instead of an independent historical expectation. Runtime baseline over the ordered _renderable_units corpus observed 884 production conversions in 32.5578s plus 884 copied legacy conversions in 32.9979s; all 884 matched and both streams had SHA-256 f44ada0854d369ce04253f530da94653196bacf0e73278a97e2028c396414b8f. Discriminating mutation: setting live _PANDOC_TO to plain changed the production digest to 8b4deccf9ca84c4e86510037c418f731ebd937e1088e199ab1edaa5ce24f1199, proving production behavior moved, yet the copied legacy digest moved identically and all 884 comparisons still passed. This rejects the alternative that the copied oracle independently pins landed bytes. Installed generator provenance is Pandoc 3.6.1 with binary SHA-256 94ebf1efbce3561379e8f25de3efe5aeabee64dc36dd8e8b9e96cf05b4195c52. Defect legitimacy: the module contract says the test proves byte identity to the landed renderer, while shared live constants make that claim false; immutable expected bytes restore the stated contract without reducing the 884 real production Pandoc calls. Separate lead: production tracing exposed repeated git root-discovery launches through per-unit timeout config loading; filed lyrical-integral-waterdogs and linked it discovered_from so it stays out of this ticket scope.
